types.name: add_correctness_unit_test
types.definition: Reviewer asks the author to add or extend unit, kernel, regression, or e2e tests that check correctness/numerical equivalence of the changed path.
types.include: Requests for kernel-vs-reference tests, model-path tests, regression tests, additional parameterized correctness cases, or adding a new test to cover the PR behavior.
types.exclude: Requests only to run existing CI/lint, provide benchmark numbers, or report model-quality evals without adding tests.
types.example: Please include unit tests. (vllm#43306)

types.name: run_accuracy_eval
types.definition: Reviewer asks for model-quality or accuracy evaluation results to show the optimization does not degrade outputs.
types.include: lm-eval, GSM8K, GPQA, MMLU, AIME, real-dataset accuracy, acceptance length when used as quality proxy, or baseline-vs-PR accuracy comparisons.
types.exclude: Kernel allclose/unit tests, generic CI, or performance benchmarks with no quality metric.
types.example: could you check lm_eval to be sure in correctness. (vllm#28095)

types.name: provide_kernel_microbenchmark
types.definition: Reviewer asks for operator/kernel-level benchmark evidence rather than whole-system serving results.
types.include: Kernel latency, bandwidth, TFLOPS, benchmark scripts under kernel benchmark directories, shape sweeps for an op, or before/after microbenchmark tables.
types.exclude: End-to-end serving throughput/latency, model-quality evals, or profiling traces without a benchmark result.
types.example: Please add a kernel micro benchmark, refer to https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/tree/main/sgl-kernel/benchmark (sglang#13049)

types.name: provide_end_to_end_benchmark
types.definition: Reviewer asks for whole-model or serving benchmark results demonstrating user-visible performance impact.
types.include: vLLM/SGLang serving benchmarks, TTFT/TPOT/ITL/throughput, real prompt workloads, larger prompt sets, higher concurrency, or model-level before/after results.
types.exclude: Isolated kernel microbenchmarks, accuracy-only evals, or reproduction commands without measured performance.
types.example: @GOavi101 can you provide some end-to-end benchmark result? (vllm#30022)

types.name: compare_against_correct_baseline
types.definition: Reviewer asks that measurements or tests use a stronger, fairer, or semantically correct baseline/comparator.
types.include: Comparisons to main, BF16 vs FP8, torch.compile/static-shape baseline, DeepGEMM/reference implementation, best non-PR backend, or before/after tables.
types.exclude: Generic requests for any benchmark, or requests for unrelated extra hardware/model coverage.
types.example: the baseline should be torch.compile with static shape, matching the production code. Comparing against eager mode is misleading (vllm#52676)

types.name: provide_reproduction_details
types.definition: Reviewer asks for enough run details to reproduce or interpret the result.
types.include: Commands, environment variables, flags, model names, dataset parameters, hardware, software/library versions, full logs, or exact benchmark settings.
types.exclude: Requests merely to update docs for users, or to add code-level comments.
types.example: can you include your env vars for AITER, shuffle KV cache, etc. in the repro command above? (vllm#52849)

types.name: provide_profile_or_trace
types.definition: Reviewer asks for profiling, traces, or evidence locating where time/overhead is spent.
types.include: Nsight/profile screenshots, kernel time traces, before/after profiler output, profiling result tables, or requests to confirm overhead reduction with a profiler.
types.exclude: Ordinary benchmark numbers without trace/profiling attribution, or code changes to reduce overhead without asking for a profile.
types.example: Please attach a screenshot of the trace file, on how the kernel time changes before and after this PR (sglang#17205)

types.name: provide_ablation_or_sensitivity
types.definition: Reviewer asks to isolate which change or workload dimension causes the effect.
types.include: Per-change ablations, sensitivity to batch size/concurrency/page size/sequence length, AVG@N to reduce variance, or sweeps needed to attribute a claimed gain.
types.exclude: A single benchmark request with no attribution/sensitivity concern, or other-hardware/model coverage coded separately.
types.example: Could we provide per-change ablation results and clarify the GPU, AITER/ROCm versions (vllm#52878)

types.name: explain_design_or_rationale
types.definition: Reviewer asks the author to justify a design choice, explain confusing behavior, or answer a substantive rationale question before approval.
types.include: Why a parameter/value/path was chosen, why an old path was removed, why a benchmark number changed, or how a proposed algorithm works.
types.exclude: Pure curiosity that does not require response/change, requests for reproduction details, or requests to add comments/docstrings to code.
types.example: What is the rationale for omitting `and chunk_m >= tp_world_size` here? (vllm#56944)

types.name: test_other_hardware_architectures
types.definition: Reviewer asks for testing or evaluation on another GPU/CPU generation, vendor, architecture, or accelerator backend.
types.include: B200/Hopper/SM90/SM100/SM120, MI300/gfx942/gfx950/gfx11, ARM/AArch64/Power/s390x, NPU/ROCm/CUDA, or multi-vendor regression checks.
types.exclude: Adding guards without testing, testing a different model on the same hardware, or TP/DP/multi-GPU modes coded separately.
types.example: Have you tested this on any other arch's to ensure this doesn't cause regression (vllm#43389)

types.name: add_hardware_backend_guard
types.definition: Reviewer asks to restrict, gate, or branch the new path by hardware/backend/platform so common paths are not affected.
types.include: CUDA/ROCm/current_platform checks, SM/gfx architecture guards, GPU arch macros, backend-specific paths, clear errors/warnings for unsupported hardware.
types.exclude: Requests only to test on other hardware, or generic feature flags not tied to hardware/backend portability.
types.example: should at least gate the changes if this is specific to rocm (vllm#46035)

types.name: handle_unsupported_shapes_dtypes_layouts
types.definition: Reviewer asks to support, guard, or explicitly handle unsupported tensor shapes, dtypes, layouts, page sizes, or special-case inputs.
types.include: Shape/dtype/layout restrictions, power-of-two assumptions, page-size 16 vs 64, contiguous/non-contiguous tensors, FP8/BF16/INT4 formats, or fallback for unsupported cases.
types.exclude: Hardware-only guards, tests on another model, or assertions that do not relate to supported input domains.
types.example: Here needs to have the condition that half_rotary_lanes is power of 2. (sglang#15141)

types.name: verify_parallelism_distributed_modes
types.definition: Reviewer asks to verify or handle distributed/parallel execution modes affected by the optimization.
types.include: TP/DP/EP/SP, multi-GPU or multi-node settings, tensor-parallel shape changes, distributed executor backends, MNNVL/allreduce modes, or guards for unsupported tp_size.
types.exclude: Single-device architecture testing, generic e2e benchmarks, or feature interactions not specifically about parallel/distributed execution.
types.example: If we can't support tp>1, we should also add a tp_size check here. (sglang#14422)

types.name: test_affected_models_or_modes
types.definition: Reviewer asks to test the optimized path on particular affected models, model families, or execution modes beyond the author's shown case.
types.include: Specific Qwen/Kimi/DeepSeek/GLM/MiniMax/VLM/diffusion models, MTP/spec-decode/prefix-cache modes, page-size modes, or model-specific command/eval requests.
types.exclude: Generic accuracy or e2e benchmarking with no named affected model/mode, and hardware-only coverage.
types.example: BTW, could you also test kimi linear? It also uses gdn attn backend (vllm#44700)

types.name: preserve_default_or_add_feature_gate
types.definition: Reviewer asks to keep existing behavior as the default or make the optimized path optional/conditional until it is proven safe.
types.include: Feature gates, opt-in/opt-out flags, disabling risky paths by default, making behavior conditional on an existing env/config, or not changing defaults for all users.
types.exclude: Naming/config API design details, hardware-specific guards, or reviewer suggestions to enable a safe path by default.
types.example: Make conditional on `envs.VLLM_MOE_SKIP_PADDING`? (vllm#46428)

types.name: design_config_api_or_env_knob
types.definition: Reviewer asks to change how a knob is exposed, named, documented, deprecated, or chosen between env vars, server args, and config fields.
types.include: Env-var vs server-arg decisions, config-field placement, flag precedence, deprecation warnings, option naming, or automatic heuristics instead of feature-specific env vars.
types.exclude: Hardware guards, simple variable renames not exposed to users, or requests merely to gate a path without discussing API surface.
types.example: Rather than an enviornment variable, lets add this to the speculative decoding config (vllm#29957)

types.name: ensure_cuda_graph_or_torch_compile_compatibility
types.definition: Reviewer asks to preserve or demonstrate compatibility with CUDA graphs, piecewise/full CUDA graphs, torch.compile, or graph-capture paths.
types.include: CUDA graph replay/capture, full decode graphs, breakable graphs, torch.compile boundaries, graph metadata, or avoiding changes that force eager mode.
types.exclude: Generic performance tests or feature gates that do not mention graph/compile compatibility.
types.example: LGTM as long as it works with torch.compile. (vllm#30885)

types.name: avoid_hot_path_overhead_or_extra_copies
types.definition: Reviewer asks to avoid adding runtime overhead on performance-critical paths.
types.include: Avoid hot-path env queries, repeated allocations, per-call workspace allocation, Python dict/object churn, unnecessary contiguous/reshape/copy, synchronization, or slow imports/checks.
types.exclude: Requests for performance evidence only, broad algorithm redesign, or memory-capacity concerns coded separately.
types.example: we should avoid consulting envvars like this on the hot path (vllm#56944)

types.name: report_or_mitigate_memory_impact
types.definition: Reviewer asks to account for memory usage, OOM risk, buffer/workspace size, or capacity side effects of the optimization.
types.include: KV-cache capacity, per-slot size inflation, double memory during weight loading, workspace buffers, peak memory, OOM concerns, or memory-savings claims.
types.exclude: Performance-only benchmarks, generic buffer assertions, or code comments about memory layout without a memory impact concern.
types.example: Convert all experts layout and stack may double the memory usage, which may cause oom when loading weights. (sglang#13798)

types.name: avoid_cross_feature_regressions
types.definition: Reviewer asks to check or fix interaction with another SGLang/vLLM feature path that might regress.
types.include: MTP/spec decode, prefix caching, async scheduling, TBO, attention backends, radix/cache paths, multimodal paths, Mamba/GDN/hybrid modes, or existing feature behavior.
types.exclude: Specific model/hardware tests without an interaction concern, or general bug fixes unrelated to feature interaction.
types.example: Does the kernel support MTP use case? (vllm#43306)

types.name: integrate_build_registration_dependencies
types.definition: Reviewer asks to integrate the optimization correctly with build systems, custom-op registration, dependency versions, or library entry points.
types.include: CMake/build-time compilation, CustomOp.register, _aiter_ops/FlashInfer registration, dependency version/commit compatibility, Dockerfile/library version checks, or avoiding ad-hoc JIT builds.
types.exclude: Moving files for code organization only, or CI failures not about integration mechanics.
types.example: All custom kernels should be compiled through build time. Not JIT build. (vllm#43306)

types.name: add_defensive_validation_assertions
types.definition: Reviewer asks to add runtime assertions, validation, or checks that make assumptions explicit and fail safely.
types.include: Asserting tensor ranks, divisibility, buffer size/device, supported K/TopK, nullability, pointer alignment, or adding validation/TODO when assumptions are unchecked.
types.exclude: Hardware/backend gates, tests that validate correctness, or user-facing config validation already coded as config API design.
types.example: Should we assert that `N % 8 == 0` (and or `BLOCK_SIZE_N`) here? (vllm#43389)

types.name: fix_functional_correctness_issue
types.definition: Reviewer identifies a concrete runtime, semantic, or correctness bug in the changed implementation and expects it to be fixed.
types.include: Wrong return values, undefined variables, signature mismatches, cache never hits, wrong tensor mutation, failing edge cases, or logic that breaks existing behavior.
types.exclude: Requests only for tests/evals, stylistic suggestions, or speculative questions without a concrete bug claim.
types.example: It looks like this cache is initialized as an empty dict on every call of this function (vllm#38061)

types.name: reuse_existing_kernel_or_utility
types.definition: Reviewer asks to reuse or extend an existing kernel, helper, wrapper, or utility instead of adding a duplicate or parallel implementation.
types.include: Unifying duplicate kernels/tests, using existing helpers, reusing wrappers, centralizing shared functions, or avoiding copied code.
types.exclude: Moving code to another module without reuse, or splitting a PR for process reasons.
types.example: Can we reuse the JIT kernel implementation? (sglang#41294)

types.name: move_code_to_proper_module
types.definition: Reviewer asks to relocate code to the repository module/library where it belongs.
types.include: Moving kernels to csrc/sgl-kernel/jit_kernel, model-specific code out of common paths, utilities to flashinfer.py/_aiter_ops, tests/benchmarks to proper directories, or backend-specific code under backend folders.
types.exclude: Build registration without relocation, or test registration/runner updates coded separately.
types.example: Move this file in to csrc, do not put source code here. (vllm#43306)

types.name: simplify_refactor_api_structure
types.definition: Reviewer asks to simplify, refactor, or redesign code/API structure for readability or maintainability.
types.include: Guard clauses, helper methods, cleaner branching, API factoring, reducing dispatch complexity, splitting functions/classes, or restructuring data flow.
types.exclude: Removing dead code, renaming only, moving files only, or broad requests to split the PR.
types.example: Can we use guard clause here to avoid nested if else? (sglang#15141)

types.name: remove_dead_redundant_debug_code
types.definition: Reviewer asks to delete unused, redundant, leftover, debug, commented-out, or no-op code or tests.
types.include: Unused variables/flags/files, redundant checks, extra tests, stale TODOs, commented logs, unnecessary format changes, no-op changes, or unreachable code.
types.exclude: Renaming/style-only issues, reducing PR scope due to unrelated features, or fixing functional bugs in live code.
types.example: `slot_mapping` is unused in this function. (vllm#58762)

types.name: naming_style_consistency
types.definition: Reviewer asks for naming, style, formatting, import, type-annotation, or coding-convention consistency.
types.include: Renaming variables/classes/flags, lower-case key conventions, import placement, type annotations, formatting nits, style consistency across backends, or clearer names.
types.exclude: User-facing config API design, comments/docstrings, or lint/pre-commit failures without a specific style request.
types.example: Rename before merge to `SGLANG_OPT_QWEN_DEEPEP_SHARED_OVERLAP` or `SGLANG_ENABLE_QWEN_DEEPEP_SHARED_OVERLAP` (sglang#34938)

types.name: add_explanatory_comments_docstrings
types.definition: Reviewer asks to add or adjust code comments, docstrings, TODOs, or inline explanations for maintainers.
types.include: Explaining nontrivial kernel algorithms, memory layouts, assumptions, class preconditions, TODO specificity, or why a workaround exists.
types.exclude: Updating user-facing docs/README/PR description, or answering a reviewer rationale question without adding code text.
types.example: can you say in the comments the format we're packing the weights to (vllm#30531)

types.name: update_docs_readme_or_pr_description
types.definition: Reviewer asks to update user-facing documentation, README files, docs pages, or the PR description.
types.include: Environment variable docs, server-arguments docs, tuning README, PR description updates, usage notes, warnings in docs, or benchmark/eval results attached to the PR description.
types.exclude: Code comments/docstrings, reproduction details requested only in a comment, or adding tests.
types.example: Please also update https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/docs/advanced_features/server_arguments.md (sglang#12787)

types.name: organize_test_or_benchmark_files
types.definition: Reviewer asks to place, register, parametrize, or consolidate test/benchmark files so they fit the repository's test infrastructure.
types.include: Adding tests to run_suite, moving tests between manual/registered/nightly directories, registering nightly tests, unifying duplicated test files, or putting benchmark scripts under the right folder.
types.exclude: Adding the substantive test itself, running CI, or moving production code.
types.example: When you add a new test file under `test/` folder, you should add it to the `run_suite.py` (sglang#12692)

types.name: reduce_pr_scope_or_split
types.definition: Reviewer asks to narrow the PR, split it, shrink the diff, or remove unrelated changes before merge.
types.include: Separate PRs for kernel/library changes, leaving unrelated build/requirement changes for later, shrinking LOC, or isolating independent optimizations.
types.exclude: Refactoring within the same scope, resolving merge conflicts, or waiting for a dependency PR.
types.example: This is not related to CPU MoE, let's leave it for another PR to make history tractable. (vllm#30531)

types.name: fix_ci_lint_precommit_or_dco
types.definition: Reviewer asks to fix automated checks or repository compliance gates before merge.
types.include: pre-commit, lint, formatting, CI failures, manually triggering CI, AMD/CUDA CI, DCO/Signed-off-by, or fixing failures the reviewer attributes to the PR/checks.
types.exclude: Adding new correctness tests, rebase requests, or reviewer statements that failures are unrelated and merge can proceed.
types.example: Can you fix the pre-commit error? (vllm#25945)

types.name: rebase_or_resolve_conflicts
types.definition: Reviewer asks the author to rebase, merge main, pull recent changes, or resolve conflicts/drift.
types.include: Rebase on latest main, update benchmarks after main changes, pull before working, resolve merge conflicts, or refresh stale branches.
types.exclude: Waiting for a prerequisite PR or splitting a PR for scope reasons.
types.example: Can you fix the pre-commit and rebase your PR from main? (vllm#27512)

types.name: resolve_dependency_or_overlapping_pr
types.definition: Reviewer asks to coordinate with prerequisite, conflicting, duplicate, or overlapping work before merge.
types.include: Do-not-merge-until another PR lands, wait for a dependency/library release, consolidate with another PR, close as superseded, or resolve conflicts with an overlapping implementation.
types.exclude: Simple rebases, reviewer-cc-only messages, or follow-up PR suggestions that do not block the current PR.
types.example: Do not merge until: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/28430 (vllm#28406)
